original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For the unsigned dirty connector of PR4231 over a ring of characteristic c, with N(c) the largest source count attaining the floor c(k+2^k-1), give one five-source depth-two walk template valid in every characteristic c>=5 and conclude N(c)>=floor(5c/2) for every c>=5 with PR4248's concatenation and deletion lemmas. Answers part of PR4248 open question 2 (growth of N(c)).
scope_change_reason: Keeps the PR4231 alphabet and increases the source count, a scope-change trigger on the card. PR4248 asked how N(c) grows and named a depth-d block with more than 2d sources valid for every large c as the route; PR4271 excludes such a depth-two block at c=4 only.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the complete-call interface floor: it raises the batch size at which a characteristic-c connector consumer can pay exactly c calls per operator. No physical consumer, admission or transfer is supplied, so no kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Stop after one uniform depth-two five-source template with an all-c proof, direct checks over a finite range of c and literal floor words for small c. Report searches for larger blocks only as search notes.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json gives a 30-event base walk and per-source cut positions. verify.py checks the integer two-prefix identity for all 31 masks (the finite core of the all-c proof), checks the expanded block directly modulo c and through the lifted readouts for every 5<=c<=64, builds the concatenated floor walks on 12, 15 and 17 sources for c=5,6,7 and simulates the literal 20,535-, 196,692- and 917,616-call words with generic coefficients, and rejects five mutation controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does any characteristic c admit a depth-two block on six or more sources, or is five the maximum for every c?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A six-source depth-two block valid for all large c would raise the lower bound to N(c)>=3c.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same lifted integer criterion on six-source base walks with several cut positions per source, or extend PR4271's depth-two counting to general c.
open_questions.blocked_by: No search or upper bound for six-source depth-two blocks is recorded here.

open_questions.question: Is there a depth-three block on eight or more sources valid for every large c?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Eight sources at depth three would give density 8/3 > 5/2 sources per readout.
open_questions.first_step: Search lifted base walks with seven or eight events per source under the integer three-prefix criterion.
open_questions.blocked_by: PR4248 reports a 125-of-127 search failure for seven sources at depth three in characteristic four only.

open_questions.question: Is N(c)/c unbounded? Counting gives N(c)=O(c log c) and this package gives N(c)>=floor(5c/2).
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether high-characteristic batches can stay at the floor with superlinear source counts.
open_questions.first_step: Look for a block family whose sources-per-depth ratio grows with depth, or a parity-type upper bound linear in c.
open_questions.blocked_by: No construction with ratio above 5/2 and no linear upper bound is known.

open_questions.question: Does any concrete consumer use a characteristic-c batch at a favorable complete invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The abstract call counts change no recursive supplier or kappa by themselves.
open_questions.first_step: Identify an immutable-source, unobserved-output caller with coefficients of characteristic c and price every primitive, admission and dispatch.
